input_narrative: SYNTHETIC NARRATIVE: Synthetic field service engineering desk reported a minor, non-recurrent complete atrioventricular block-adjacent irregularity with no adverse patient outcome recorded. The bedside monitor log and the cloud-side classifier log disagree on whether the irregularity met the complete atrioventricular block detection threshold, an unresolved discordance. The case is being handled at a monitoring/investigation level, not as a confirmed life-threatening event.

risk_report.rationale: The incident describes a non-recurrent discordance between bedside monitor logs and cloud-side classifier logs regarding complete atrioventricular block detection thresholds. No adverse patient outcome was recorded, indicating the event did not result in realized harm or missed clinical alerting that impacted patient safety (Severity Dimension A: None). The narrative explicitly states the case is being handled at a monitoring/investigation level rather than as a confirmed life-threatening event, suggesting containment by existing operational processes before any serious exposure occurred (Severity Dimension C: Contained/Investigated). While there is technical regression evidence in test logs for releases v23 and v27, these represent internal validation artifacts showing the detection failure; without data on patient population size or historical recurrence of similar failures, we cannot confirm broad deployed-population impact. The lack of specific timestamps from bedside monitors or cloud-side decision boundaries prevents a definitive causal link to clinical harm in this specific instance (Severity Dimension B: Unclear potential). Therefore, severity is assigned as 1 because the event was contained/investigated with no patient exposure.
